mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when GDP growth rate is high.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which leads to lower stock prices and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when the federal funds rate is above 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to lower consumer spending and subsequently drives down the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the unemployment rate is rising.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher stock prices and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when industrial production is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the housing market is strong, as indicated by an increase in housing starts, and the GDP growth rate is also high, it leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both housing starts and GDP growth rate are high.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low and the inflation rate is also low, it indicates a loose monetary policy, which leads to higher stock prices and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when both the federal funds rate and inflation rate are low.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and the payroll employment is also increasing, it indicates a strong labor market, which leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the retail sales are strong, as indicated by an increase in RSAFS, and the GDP growth rate is also high, it leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days, but only during the holiday season.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both retail sales and GDP growth rate are high during the holiday season.
